tool_arguments.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: exactly one finished opaque landscape 4:3 architectural poster, aiming for 2048×1536, part of the same cheerful illustrated Moscow series as Image 2.

Input images:
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the existing poster for this place. Retain the recognizable architectural identity, series index and exact location wording.
Image 2 is the USER-APPROVED PRIMARY STYLE REFERENCE: the bright Mossovet poster. Transfer its sunny warm paper, delicate gouache and screenprint texture, vermilion display lettering, luminous turquoise and green shadows, observed architectural detail, humane narrative figures and optimistic daylight. Do not copy the Mossovet building, its place names, its pioneer characters or its tiny signature-like mark.
Image 3 is the original PHOTOGRAPH OF THIS BUILDING: use it as an architectural identity check. Preserve actual connected roof forms, facade rhythms and the original viewpoint. Remove the photographic traffic, signs, wires and unrelated urban clutter.

Series visual language: A professionally art-directed mid-century painted poster, warm and alive, with an illustrated real building as the dominant subject. Use luminous warm ivory or butter-yellow fields, red and ochre masonry where present, gentle green/turquoise shadows, and careful small narrative figures. Keep substantial light negative space and confident Cyrillic block lettering. Paper grain is delicate rather than distressed; faces and hands are naturally drawn. Architecture and people belong in one coherent perspective and light. Avoid large near-black fields, heavy gritty halftone, photorealistic cutout people or theatrical gloom.

Primary request: Reimagine the Church of the Transfiguration in Bogorodskoye as a joyful, tender spring Easter poster with families and pussy-willow branches. Carry over the approved Mossovet's warmth and painted character, while letting this be a peaceful family and church scene with no Soviet uniform motifs.

Scene and architectural treatment: Fresh spring morning, gentle golden sunlight, a warm ivory sky with pale blue air and soft light clouds. Early green leaves, tender grass at the path and restrained willow twigs establish spring. The actual wooden church is luminous soft rose and peach, with delicate clean white carved trim, dark sage-green roofs and modest gold dome highlights. Keep all three unequal roof accents with their original crosses, the open central belfry and bell, left gabled entrance, connected long windowed right wing and the original oblique perspective. Preserve real shapes and wooden-board rhythm. Remove the old temporary canopy and urban background; keep the true steps and entrance.

Human narrative: Two small family groups in the foreground make a warm intergenerational scene: parents with children and a grandmother, quietly walking toward the church or greeting one another. Naturally proportioned painted figures in modest spring coats, light scarves and ordinary festive clothes. A parent holds a child's hand; the grandmother and one child hold slim pussy-willow branches with clearly visible soft SILVERY-GREY CATKINS on brown twigs, not yellow mimosa balls or palm leaves. One small wicker Easter basket with a white cloth, a modest iced kulich and a few red-dyed eggs makes Easter visible. Keep the basket secondary and in scale. Gentle smiles and caring gestures, no posed mass procession. A few foreground willow twigs may softly frame a lower corner without obscuring the lettering or church. This is a locally rooted Orthodox spring family scene, not a generic commercial holiday illustration; no Easter rabbits or fantasy chapel.

Typography and composition: Use large warm vermilion Cyrillic БОГОРОДСКОЕ, broadly placed behind the authentic roof silhouette as in the existing poster, and the same serif 01 index as the rest of the series. Keep the district caption and full small church name and street address clearly readable in dark green on a light lower area. Place the family groups in the foreground beside the path, leaving the architecture dominant, its three roof tops unobscured and all small text clear. Maintain the tactile painted and softly printed quality of Image 2, with a distinctly spring pink/green/cream palette and joyful spiritual calm.

Text (verbatim):
01
МОСКВА · БОГОРОДСКОЕ
БОГОРОДСКОЕ
Храм Преображения
Краснобогатырская улица, 17

Identity invariants: Three unequal roof accents with their correct crosses; open central belfry with a bell; authentic gabled entrance and connected right wing; white carved wooden trim; original oblique viewpoint and roof proportions.

Final constraints: Only the listed Cyrillic text and actual source building inscriptions may appear. No extra dates, slogans, names, reference labels, watermarks, artist initials, signatures or illegible micro-writing anywhere. The added people, objects and surrounding atmosphere are clearly illustrative narrative, not a claimed archival reconstruction. Preserve enough real architecture to identify the exact site, and keep ordinary anatomy and integrated scale. Deliver one coherent cheerful landscape poster, not a collage of rectangular photographs.

reference_use: Approved bright Mossovet as overall series art direction.
